The co-Lip predicate contains both U.Nonempty and U⊆dom, with the lower inequality on every pair and output. The empty-domain family is proved empty.
entry M i j is M j i; both the display example and multiplication expansion preserve input/output orientation and application order.
Channels are ordered pairs. The row predicate permits any single input, and the displayed diagonal equivalence is proved; zero coefficients are removed only from this certificate sum.
The finite sum is proved equal to its selected input term, then the original Lip inequality is transported; the diagonal case is included.
A single nonnegative summand is bounded by the whole co-Lip sum; positivity in ENNReal covers infinite coefficients and distances without an unjustified finiteness assumption.
The proof concludes GaugeZeroRelated, never point equality. The optional nonseparating Option Bool example satisfies all metric/domain/co-Lip premises and refutes point-equality strengthening.
The lower bound uses only the selected co-Lip summand, and the upper bound uses Lip row sparsity. No co-Lip sparsity has been added.

All possible scalar certificates contradict the zero-input/positive-output pair, so the family is empty and its infimum top.

Every diagonal row supplies its own scalar Lip bound.
Only the Lip row is sparse; the co-Lip diagonal summand gives the lower scalar bound without extra lower sparsity.
All components are combined, and finite diagonal coefficients are explicitly represented by NNReal values under the additional finiteness premise.
The selected positive co-Lip summand proves positive output distance; coefficients need not be finite.
A zero output family contradicts every possible positive input distance, yielding exactly family-zero distance, not point equality.
